One whose complexion is blazing like the rising sun, whose body is adorned with jewels, and who remains for the duration of an eon—having empowered [this] eight thousand times, one may enter into the midst of enemies; no fear shall arise, and one shall be invincible.

One effects the possession of all enemies with a white flower; one causes dancing by means of water over which the mantra has been recited three times; one brings [them] under control with a *karavīra* flower over which the mantra has been recited three times. It reveals the past and the future. Binding is released by a snap of the fingers. One desiring to prepare the collyrium (*añjana*) should take *sauvīra* collyrium purchased from a hero, remove its impurities, and [proceed].

One should grind [the ingredients] with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) using the ring finger. Having formed four pills, one should cover them with a lotus leaf and dry them. In front of the cloth painting (paṭa), having duly kindled a fire and performed a thousand oblations (sahasrasampātāhuti), one should perform a grand worship at a reliquary (caitya) containing relics, while facing the eight directions.

Having kindled a fire with *palāśa* wood, one should place it at the hip region; thus the binding of semen (*śukrabandha*) is accomplished. Having made a knot with the corner of a robe (*cīvarakarṇaka*) over which the mantra has been recited seven times, there is the binding of poison (*viṣabandha*). This is the treatment for poison. By means of a sprout and the breaking of the seal, possession is induced by water. With *guggulu* incense or water, there is the binding of planetary spirits (*grahabandha*). [One should touch] the finger...

Having recited [the mantra] over it, whoever one threatens becomes submissive. One should recite it eight hundred times before the cloth painting (*paṭa*); it will show things exactly as they are in a dream. Having installed the painting before a reliquary (*caitya*) containing relics, and having performed a grand worship before it, [one should offer] white lotuses smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, [and kindle] a fire with *vilva* wood.
Having kindled [the fire], one should offer a hundred thousand oblations; one obtains a kingdom. If it is not accomplished, by offering a thousand lumps [of food], one obtains a village.

One should recite [the mantra] a thousand times before a cloth-painting (paṭa) while holding either gorocanā or realgar. Having applied a tilaka-mark with that, one obtains whatever one seeks. On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for one night, at night...

One should offer eight thousand oblations into a fire of cotton-seed husks and wool; one obtains a thousand gold coins (*rūpaka*). Having fasted for a day and night on the eighth day of the bright fortnight, one should descend into a river flowing to the ocean and offer ten thousand lotuses; one obtains a kingdom. For the subjugation of a man, [one should act] on the eighth day of the dark fortnight.

Having fasted for three nights and kindled a fire with wood from the Bodhi tree, one should offer eight thousand *kumuda* flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee; [the target] becomes submissive. To subjugate a woman, one should strike the noble Mañjuśrī with *saugandhika* flowers on the twelfth day of the dark fortnight.

With the intent of binding medicinal herbs, she shall drive away bipeds and quadrupeds. Day by day, she shall give five dīnāras; they must not be spent on anything else. Half [of the proceeds] shall be for the use of the Three Jewels. For one month before the cloth painting, twelve thousand dānāras shall be given.
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, one should recite [the mantra]. On the eighth day of the dark fortnight, it bestows sovereignty (*rājya*).
Having consecrated a ritual stake (*kīlaka*) eight thousand times, one should [recite] over each individual segment twenty-one times.
Having recited [the mantra] and cast it into the fire, one obtains hundreds of dīnāras at dawn.
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, having fasted for one night, one should offer eight thousand *atimuktaka* flowers for seven days;
one obtains a hundred dīnāras. One should recite [the mantra] over eyes that have not been anointed with collyrium for seven days; one becomes beloved by all people.

Having consecrated common collyrium with mantras, whoever one first sees becomes subject to one's will. Reciting ten thousand times before a cloth painting while focusing on a specific person [brings them under control]. One should recite one hundred thousand times at the entrance of a cave. Or, having established a caitya containing the essence of dependent origination (pratītyasamutpāda) on a mountain peak or in a cow-pen, one should recite one hundred thousand times as prescribed.

One obtains one hundred thousand dīnāras. Having installed the cloth-painting in a place of the nāgas and having performed the well-prepared ritual of protection, one should kindle a fire with jambuka wood, offer a bali-oblation of the three sweets, and perform eight thousand oblations of nāgapuṣpa flowers. Then the Nāga King arrives in the form of a Brāhmaṇa, and he...
He says: "And you must say, 'Give seven dīnāras every day. Having said, 'So be it,' he becomes invisible.

To subjugate a general, one should smear a large mandala, take the dust from his footprints, and offer a thousand oblations with the left hand; he becomes subjugated. For the subjugation of an ordinary woman, [use] salt."

Having fashioned an effigy and repeatedly cutting it with the left hand, one should offer it as an oblation; [the person] becomes submissive. Furthermore, for the subjugation of a female slave, one should combine *punnāga* stamens, barley, and wheat, and offer eight thousand oblations; she becomes submissive. Having fashioned an effigy made of rice flour and repeatedly cutting it, one should offer it as an oblation; [the person] becomes submissive.

To subjugate a widow, one should offer oblations of *māṣa* beans and *jambū* fruit; she will become submissive. If one takes *śrotāñjana* (antimony) and places it between the leaves of an *aśvattha* tree at a single caitya, having consecrated it eight thousand times, and practices this again, one’s lifespan becomes doubled. Having entered a granary, having established the cloth-painting (*paṭa*) in a clean place, one should remain silent.

Subsisting on a diet of milk and barley gruel, one should recite [the mantra] for one fortnight. Then, having performed an elaborate worship of the cloth painting and having offered a most magnificent *bali* offering, one should sit in the *paryaṅka* posture and recite until rays of light issue forth.
Upon seeing them, even the five sins of immediate retribution (*ānantarya*) reach exhaustion. Thereafter, one becomes accomplished; [one attains] great sovereignty.

One obtains [the desired result]. One becomes one who seeks the deathless (*amṛta*). Having consecrated yellow pigment (*rocanā*) eight thousand times with mantras and having fumigated it with incense, one should place it between the teeth; one then becomes a speaker of truth, and all become subject to one’s will.
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, having fasted for three nights, one should recite the mantra eight thousand times before the cloth painting (*paṭa*). [The rest follows as before.]
On the fourteenth day, one should offer incense of *guggulu* before the cloth painting for three nights.
Then, one should see realgar (*manaḥśilā*) resembling a *karavīra* flower at the site of the fire-pit (*agnikuṇḍa*), which is the size of a lotus.
While reciting the mantra, it should be taken up. Having been thus taken up, one becomes a *vidyādhara*, possessing the complexion of the rising sun and the appearance of a sixteen-year-old.
By virtue of being equal to the wind, desired foods arise [spontaneously]. For eighty thousand years...
It remains alive; it is inaccessible to all beings and brings about death. One should perform the rite before a painted image (*paṭa*);

by casting [the substance] into one's mouth, one becomes invisible. First, the release from bondage must be performed: having fashioned an effigy out of honey and beeswax—whether of a woman or a man—one should kindle a fire in a secluded place and consecrate it with the mantra.

One should cause [the offering] to be given. Having pierced [the object] one hundred and eight times with a *madanakaṇṭaka* thorn, one should cause it to be given; they become submissive. Whatever one prays for, that one obtains. On the full moon of the bright fortnight, having fasted for a day and night, one should present one hundred and eight fragrant flowers; one obtains five *kārṣāpaṇas*. On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for a day and night...

Having kindled a fire before the cloth painting with *priyaṅgu* wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *vaikaṅkata* fuel-sticks. By means of [water] consecrated a hundred times, one pacifies all colic. For a woman in difficult labor, one should give water that has been consecrated eight hundred times; this causes her to give birth easily.
Beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight, one should recite [the mantra] with an increase of one thousand repetitions each day until the fifteenth day.
At the conclusion, having fasted for three nights, one should prepare a pill by means of the *gulikā*-method; having consecrated it and placed it in the mouth, one becomes invisible.
[The ingredients are: a blue *aśoka* flower, the bile of a black antelope (*kṛṣṇasāra*), the heart of a ruddy goose (*cakravāka*), together with the fat of a Vedic scholar (*śrotriya*).

One should wrap equal portions [of the substances] with *puṣpaloha* (flower-metal). Having again wrapped it with the three metals (*triloha*), one who desires to accomplish [the rite] should place a cloth-painting (*paṭa*) right there in front of a statue containing relics (*sadhātupratimā*). On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, having performed worship and placed [the object] upon seven *aśvattha* leaves, one should prepare a mandala and, in its center, a man whose limbs are uninjured.

Having established himself and protected himself with the mantra, he should step upon [the person's] chest with his left foot and recite the mantra until [the person] rises as before. Then, one should feed them honeyed milk-rice (*madhupāyasa*). Having formed a fist over which the mantra has been empowered seven times, it should be struck against the head. Thereupon, the person vomits; having drunk that, one becomes invisible. One who has fasted for three nights [should perform this] during a lunar eclipse (*somagraha*).
Having entered the water up to the navel, one should recite [the mantra] until [the sound] "ka" is heard; one obtains one hundred dīnāras.

If one repeats it, one obtains auspicious things. Having bathed with salt and cow-urine water eight hundred times, having applied ointment, and having worshipped with perfumes and garlands, [one should take] a handful of dūrvā grass [recited] seven times.

Having placed it upon the head, one should strike it; then, one becomes a Vidyādhara who remains for a great eon (*mahākalpa*). Having empowered [the object] with the arrow... one should strike it. Gold [obtained through] a thousand piercings...
one should perform [the rite] upon the body... even one who has committed the five acts of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*) attains success.

By means of one hundred thousand *caityas*, one becomes a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) of the *vidyādharas*. He is proficient in all scriptures, endowed with all specialized knowledge, and remains for the duration of a *kalpa*. Even when he passes away, he does not go to the lower realms for five hundred lifetimes; he is born in the most exalted central regions.

Endowed with all the sense faculties, possessing a retentive memory for what he has heard, and remembering his past lives, he should take mind-stone (manaḥśilā) obtained without asking, place it upon seven leaves of the holy fig tree (*aśvattha*), and perform the rite. At twilight, all those who hear or smell it become submissive. He emerges, having pierced through mountains, walls, and the ocean. [This is to be done] in a cremation ground.

Having smeared a mandala measuring sixteen cubits or eight cubits, one should place the corpse with its head toward the north, insert a finger into its mouth, and step upon its chest with the right foot; one should recite the mantra until the corpse moves. Then, grasping that finger with one's hand, it gives [the desired object].

Having placed it on the ring finger, whoever he commands comes; saying "Return," he causes him to return. Having brought a corpse with uninjured limbs and placing his foot upon the corpse, he should recite the mantra until it stands up. Having performed this, one should write the mantra there with saffron on the eighth day of the dark fortnight.

On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having observed the *poṣadha* vows and remaining firm in his observances, he should go alone— without anyone else— to a mountain peak; avoiding the guardians of the directions, he should smear a mandala eight cubits in size and fashion a stupa made of sand, perform worship according to his ability, and face the east.
Holding a sword with his right hand and raising his arm, he should recite the mantra in front of a *caitya* until the syllables vanish. Having grasped that leaf, which has become a blazing sword,
he becomes a *vidyādhara* who travels wherever he desires and is invulnerable to all *vidyādharas* and all sentient beings.

He becomes invincible, able to assume any form at will, and remains for an eon; he sees for a thousand *yojanas*. With reed leaves smeared with pungent oil, there is the pacification of the earth; with rice from a *śāli* field, the attainment of mountains. With mustard seeds over which the mantra has been recited one hundred thousand times, he destroys the mantras of the *āsuras*. With an arrow over which the mantra has been recited eight hundred times, he [destroys] thunderbolts, diamonds, stones, and so forth, wherever he desires.

In that regard, one causes [an enemy] to fall by scattering ashes consecrated with seven recitations in whichever direction one casts them; there, a barrier of arrows is created. By means of one hundred and eight recitations, all shafts are extracted. Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), one should recite twenty-five lakhs before the cloth painting (*paṭa*). Then, a sword made from palm-leaf that can be cut with the fingernails—

For the protection of all crops from bipeds, quadrupeds, insects, mice, and so forth, one should empower [the substance] eight thousand times with mantras and scatter it; he becomes invulnerable to all *nāgas*. By reciting [the mantra] one hundred thousand times, he liberates [beings] from whatever [bondage]. During a solar eclipse, [one should take] the ghee of a cow that has a calf of the same age...
In a copper vessel, one should recite [the mantra] until [it bubbles]; having drunk that, one is released from all diseases by means of the previously mentioned rite involving the relic.

At a *caitya*, one who has observed the *poṣadha* vow should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *śrīpiṣṭa* mixed with *sarjarasa*; he will obtain a thousand *dīnāras*. One should offer eight thousand white mustard seeds smeared with ghee; then she reveals a treasure, which should be taken. This should be done at a *caitya* containing relics located on a river flowing to the ocean.
Or, having constructed a stūpa one Sugata-span in height, containing the essence of dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), out of sand from a river;

being pure and observing the *poṣadha* vows, and having performed worship according to one's ability, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times while subsisting on alms-food or sacrificial food (*haviṣya*). One becomes capable of all rites by means of a great cemetery collection.
It performs the binding of the cardinal and intermediate directions starting from the mandala; it is a remedy for all poisons, and it destroys afflictions caused by spirits and fever.

One should recite it when crossing a great river, and one crosses with ease. By mere recitation, one becomes honored by ferrymen, tax collectors, and border guards. In a dispute, one becomes the winner of the case. By means of [the water] used for sleep-inducing, semen-binding, or urine-binding, if recited one thousand times—
With eight thousand recitations over *khadira* wood pegs, one does not [succeed] in the subjugation by mantra.

Having made an image of butter the size of a thumb-joint out of barley grains smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, and having placed it upon an *aśvattha* leaf, one should hold it with the hand and recite the mantra until it vibrates; then, without touching it with the teeth—
One should grasp [the mantra]. At that very moment, she arrives in a beautiful form and becomes the granter of all desires.

Having kindled a fire with *vilva* wood, one should offer ten thousand oblations of *vilva* fuel-sticks; thus one obtains enjoyments. In all ritual procedures, this constitutes a protective circle (*maṇḍalabandha*) against thieves, tigers, crocodiles, sharks, and water-monsters.

The binding of the boundary is the binding of the mouth. Regarding the acquisition of treasure: having gone to the place where the treasure is located, one should fast there, smear a mandala, kindle a fire with wood from the *bilva* tree, and offer oblations of royal mustard seeds (*rājasarṣapa*). One obtains the treasure. If one desires to bring under control the queen together with her retinue, [one should fashion] an image made of *kuśa* grass...
Having made an image and grasping it with the left hand, one should recite [the mantra] one thousand times; she, together with her retinue, will become submissive.

For the subjugation of a Brahmin, one should offer eight thousand oblations of sesame seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, and he, together with his retinue, will be subdued. For the subjugation of a Kṣatriya, one should offer eight thousand oblations of barley smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.

He becomes submissive along with his retinue. For the subjugation of a Vaiśya, one should offer eight thousand oblations of black mustard seeds; he becomes submissive along with his retinue. For the subjugation of a Śūdra, one should offer eight thousand oblations of the husks of black rice;
he becomes submissive. The oblation should be performed alone for three days. [The offering material] is the ghee of that very same tawny cow.

Having combined [the materials], one should offer seven oblations of *mālatī*. One should place white mustard seeds consecrated seven times upon the head; he becomes submissive. One should recite [the mantra] over a king...
he becomes... Having consecrated a sword, one should wear it at the waist.
(From *pdf* 166, p.
711) Then, having had the cowherd perform the protection ritual, one should have the cow milked. Then, in a secluded place, one should recite the mantra over that milk while it is in a jar.
Then, having stirred it, [one should add] lotus seeds, *tagara*, lotus filaments, and sandalwood by means of a Brahmin girl.

One should grind it with honey. Having made a pill and consecrated it while together with betel leaf, whoever one gives it to becomes submissive. Having recited the mantra over a garland of flowers, whoever one places upon their head becomes submissive.
[Likewise] red sandalwood, campaka flowers, and lotus filaments...

Having combined equal parts of red rice husks, *girikarṇikā*, seeds of *koraṇḍaka*, rice, black gram (*māṣa*), *kuṣṭha*, *tagara*, and *turuṣka* oil, one should kindle a fire with *jāti* wood and offer eight thousand oblations of *jāti* flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. One obtains five hundred *dīnāras*.

Having kindled a fire with mango wood on a riverbank, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *arka* fuel-sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. On the fifth day, one obtains five *dīnāras*. Beginning from the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight until the fifteenth, one should offer oblations of *aśoka* fuel-sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.

One should offer eight thousand oblations; one obtains a hundred dīnāras. Having kindled a fire with *karavīra* wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *karavīra* creepers. Beginning on the eighth day of the bright fortnight until the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, one obtains a thousand dīnāras; one should offer eight thousand oblations every day.

"Until the fourteenth day": one who has performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*) should appease an enraged royal family—like an angry friend—by means of various rituals. Having fasted for three nights and having obtained a piece of wood six finger-breadths long from a tree struck by lightning, he should recite the mantra over it.
Then, having installed the cloth painting (*paṭa*) in a reliquary shrine (*caitya*) containing sacred relics, he should bind that ritual stake (*kīlaka*) with the three metals.

One should place four jars filled with all kinds of medicinal herbs upon a bed of lotuses. Having stepped upon that stake with the left foot and grasped it with the left hand, one should recite the mantra until it vanishes, without letting go of the hand. Then, one should offer a great bali-oblation. At dawn, one should eat a pomegranate. That stake—

Success is achieved. One should bury it in a forest, and it becomes a house that grants all desires; all necessary implements also appear there. When it is dug up, everyone should drink from it and bathe; then again, this same ritual procedure is to be followed for as long as the entire night lasts. At dawn, the monks designated for the Saṅgha should be fed, and having fed them—

One should eat pomegranates that have been soaked in ghee. [The mantra] does not come; the fourteen branches of knowledge enter one’s mouth. One becomes a possessor of the power of retention (*śrutidhara*). Having descended into a river flowing toward the ocean and forming a fist with the right hand, one should recite it for thirteen days. It revives all those bitten by venomous creatures by means of the fist.
It destroys everything.
(pdf 167, p.
712) Being released by one's own will, having stayed for three nights beneath an *aśoka* tree, [one should recite] eight thousand [times] of *marīca* [mantras].
One should offer oblations. Having placed a single grain of black pepper in one's mouth, if one gazes with unblinking eyes, that person becomes submissive.

By mere recollection, one destroys all calamities. If there is a woman who does not please one, having taken her name and consecrated clarified butter with the mantra, one should cause it to be given to her; she will become well-disposed. This is the Vajra-sādhana. A vajra made of *puṣpaloha* (flower-metal).

Having fashioned a three-pronged [needle] sixteen finger-breadths in length, one should descend to a river flowing to the ocean and offer a hundred thousand fragrant flowers. The final flower returns, having pierced its way against the current;
one should swallow it without touching it with the teeth. Day by day, one will grasp five hundred knots [of scripture]. This is for one who has performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*).

One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times before the cloth painting (*paṭa*). Then, having gone to the place where the treasure is located, one should smear a jar made of *kālamūlaka* wood with all kinds of perfumes and fill it with water infused with white sandalwood. Having consecrated it eight thousand times, one should place it at the site of the treasure;
the entire ground will burst open, and the treasure will be found at a depth of one man’s height.

It remains. It should be grasped. One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of *palāśa* fuel-sticks; one obtains a thousand cows. One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of *śephālikā* flowers; one obtains a kingdom. One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of *arka* fuel-sticks; one obtains a thousand *dīnāra*s. One should offer oblations of fresh butter; one obtains five villages.

One should offer a hundred thousand *piṇḍāraka* flowers; one obtains four crores of *phaṭṭaka* garments. One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of milk; one obtains a hundred *vitarka* garments. One should offer a hundred thousand *kumuda* flowers; one obtains a wife together with gold. One should offer a hundred thousand *piṇḍāraka* flowers.

Having ascended a mountain peak, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times. In whatever country one recites it, the king of that country will attend upon one as a son. One should offer oblations of lotuses marked with the syllable *Śrī*; the glory of lotuses will come to one.
One who desires the power of recitation should daily offer curd; then recitation becomes constant. One who desires nourishment should offer ghee; the attainment of wealth occurs.
One who is pure at all times [attains success] in five nights; a king in seven nights; piśācas in nine nights;
yakṣas and rākṣasas in twelve nights; the kings of the nāgas in half a month;
apsarases in twenty-one days; and gods, dānavas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and divine beings in thirty nights.
To subjugate all the retinues and the wives of kings, one should offer eight thousand oblations [of *surasa*].
She becomes submissive. One should offer [oblations] of *raktakarata*... one obtains a princess.
[Of] *bilva*-anointed [seeds], [a result] arises. [Of] *śatapuṣpā* flowers anointed with...

One should offer one hundred thousand oblations; one obtains a hundred [gold pieces]. Having prepared eight thousand pieces of black salt (*sauvarcala*), one who has anointed their eyes with it brings all sentient beings under control.
Having recited [the mantra] over perfumes, one should offer them as an oblation; this brings all beings under control. Having recited [the mantra] over a form, one should fumigate oneself;
this brings all beings under control. Having recited [the mantra] over the topknot, one should bind it; this provides protection everywhere and paralyzes all beings.
One who desires to bring a widow under control should offer mung beans as an oblation. All...
They become submissive. One who desires to bring a yakṣiṇī under control should offer eight thousand lotuses as oblations;

she comes within three nights. If she does not come then, she comes within seven nights. She becomes a granter of boons; one should seek whatever is desired. One who desires a maiden should offer a hundred thousand oblations; he obtains the maiden of his choice. Now...

One desiring to accomplish the Vetāla should take a corpse with its limbs unbroken, and having offered an oblation of all kinds of spirits (*sarvabhūtika*) at a cremation ground, or under a solitary tree, or at a crossroads, or at a single *liṅga*, he should smear a mandala before the right-facing form of Mahādeva,
present the offering, and having bathed and adorned [the corpse], he should [mark] the mandala with ashes.

Having drawn [the image] and placed it with its head facing east, the practitioner, covered by a white cloth and accompanied by companions dressed in white garments, should station the guardians of the directions. Sitting upon a prepared seat, he should offer oblations of sesame and mustard seeds into its mouth until the jewel emerges from its mouth. Having seized it, for himself—
Having cast [the substance] into his mouth and offered a *bali* for all beings, he stood before the Right-faced Form (*dakṣiṇamūrti*).

Taking a single portion of yellow orpiment, red arsenic, collyrium, madder, and yellow pigment (*rocanā*), and having placed it between leaves of the holy fig tree (*aśvattha*), he should recite the mantra until the threefold accomplishment occurs: it steams, smokes, and blazes. While it is steaming...

By practicing it while walking on foot, one attains a lifespan of five thousand years and gains the power to subjugate all sentient beings. When smoke issues forth, one becomes invisible and attains a lifespan of ten thousand years. When it blazes with flames, one becomes a master of all vidyādharas;
reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times above [the fire], one becomes the lord of all vidyādharas and remains for an eon.

One becomes possessed of the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijña*). There is binding above, below, and of the guardians of the directions. One becomes most beloved in the royal court and one’s speech is authoritative. If one desires a maiden, one should offer eight thousand *jātī* flowers; one obtains a maiden. With those very same flowers when they have blossomed, there is the attainment of a woman.
By means of the *sarvagrahamudrā*, with speech, with a message, or with *rocanā*, one paralyzes fire; one paralyzes ships;
one attracts [beings], and causes one who is bitten or not bitten to enter [possession]; one raises the dead; and by means of speech, one dispatches fever.
One who subsists on rice cooked in milk and red lac (*yāvaka*) should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times while wearing clean clothes and having performed the threefold ritual installation.

Having placed [the object] upon a *liṅga* containing the practitioner (*sādhaka*), and having performed a great worship, one should recite [the mantra] an immeasurable number of times. All children will become submissive. One should also perform [this]. One should cause water consecrated by reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times to be given to cows; it pacifies disease. Having fasted for a day and night, [one should take up] a sword...

Having fashioned a sword from *khadira* wood, one should recite [the mantra] on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight at a cremation ground until it blazes. By grasping it, one becomes a *vidyādhara* with unimpeded movement and possesses hair that is curled into locks.

He shall remain for an eon and be highly esteemed by all the vidyādharas. Alternatively, having performed the preliminary rites (puraścaraṇa) during an eclipse of the moon or sun, one should rise at dawn, perform worship of the cloth painting (paṭa), and feed the monks with gifts;
thus one should seek success. Thereafter, one becomes successful in even more exalted rites.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of *dūrvā* sprouts smeared with curds, honey, and ghee;

this liberates from bondage. Furthermore, having consecrated a sword eight thousand times with mantras, one should place it at the entrance of a cave, a temple, or a city; having shattered the door-panel, it flings open the gate.
By reciting it once, one achieves self-protection. By offerings of milk, women become submissive. Mentally, one establishes two mantras;

one paralyzes all mudrās and pulverizes all mantras. One brings the daughters of the asuras under control. By offering a hundred oblations of all types of perfumes, women of noble family become submissive.

By the offering of the remains of divine worship (*devanirmālya*), deities, temple attendants (*taṭika*), and renunciants become submissive. Placing the hand upon the heart, one should recite [the mantra];
this destroys all sins and attracts all sentient beings. Placing the hand upon the head, one should recite it one hundred and eight times;
this paralyzes all sentient beings and destroys sin. Having consecrated a *bilva* fruit with the recitation, one attracts all sentient beings.

In the practice of the *śikhā*, one should recite the mantra beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight until the twilight. Then, having consecrated the *śikhā* with eight thousand recitations, one should go for alms at the houses of Brāhmaṇas. When one no longer sees anyone giving alms, then one has attained success (*siddha*). On the first day, there is one alms-offering; and so on, in this manner.

For seven days; on the twenty-first day, it succeeds even for one who is devoid of merit. During a lunar eclipse, having consecrated milk with the mantra, one should drink it; it becomes a great elixir (*rasāyana*). Having consecrated a handful of water twenty-one times, if one throws it toward the house of someone for seven days, that person becomes submissive. A handful of water...

Having consecrated it seven times with mantras, whoever drinks it becomes submissive. By looking at someone while reciting the mantra twenty-one times, whoever one looks upon becomes submissive. By performing a hundred thousand oblations of *guggulu* resin, one obtains a kingdom.
By offering or burning blue lotuses (*utpala*), white water lilies (*kumuda*), white lotuses (*puṇḍarīka*), and so forth, whatever one desires [is attained].
One brings [others] under one's control. A breach in a wall is made with food; or a binding of the topknot is made with pebbles in water.
Taking natural collyrium and reciting the mantra twenty-one times, one should apply it as eye-salve; one becomes beloved by all people.
The ingredients for the salve are tagara, kuṣṭha, vacā, lotus filaments, gorocanā, and manmatha.

Having made an image [of the deity] out of eight thousand [units of material] and having installed it with four *aśvattha* leaves, one should recite [the mantra] until [the desired result] is attained; one becomes beloved by all. (pdf 170, p.

One should swallow it without touching it with the teeth. Immediately upon swallowing it, whatever one contemplates arises entirely. One becomes able to assume any form at will and gains the strength of ten men. Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), on the full moon day, one who has fasted for three nights should perform worship with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings before a cloth painting (*paṭa*) and at a reliquary (*caitya*) containing sacred relics.

Having placed a sword made of *kuśa* grass upon a leaf of the *aśvattha* tree, one should grasp it by the hilt until it vibrates. Having grasped it, one becomes a *vidyādhara*. In front of the cloth painting, during the fortnight of miracles (*prātihārakapakṣa*), bathing three times a day, changing one's clothes three times, and reciting the mantra eight thousand times at the three junctions of the day—until the full moon.
Having fasted for three nights, one should prepare a *saṅghāṭī* robe, smear it with all kinds of fragrances,
and light eight thousand ghee lamps. Seated in the *paryaṅka* posture, having smeared a mandala with perfumes and placed the *saṅghāṭī* upon it,
one should step upon it with the left hand and recite the mantra until it flies up.
He stands at a height of seven palm trees. Having paid homage to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas with this very mantra, it should be taken up. As soon as it is taken up, one becomes a Vidyādhara;
all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and so forth, pay him obeisance before the cloth painting.

Having offered various oblations and performed a magnificent worship, one should place *rocanā* on a lotus leaf and, seated in the *paryaṅka* posture, recite the mantra until the threefold accomplishment is attained. When it becomes warm, there is the subjugation of all sentient beings, and one lives for a thousand years. When it emits smoke, [one lives] for thousands of millions of years.
He lives; he travels a thousand *yojanas* and returns by that same way. Unwearied, he becomes invisible to all the *siddhas* by means of his mind.
He produces food by means of his mind. Then he blazes with the color of the risen sun, appearing as a youth of sixteen years, with hair curled and coiled like a ringlet, remaining for an entire eon.

Surrounded by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of vidyādharas, he goes wherever he desires. For one who has performed the preliminary rites (puraścaraṇa), the signs of success are the swaying of the flower garland, the increasing of the lamp flame, the emission of rays of light, and the trembling of the cloth-painting (paṭa). Having seen these, whatever he seeks to accomplish is achieved, and there is the destruction of his sins.
Desiring to bring under one's control the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas,

one should kindle a fire with charcoal from khadira wood before the cloth painting and offer eight thousand oblations of salt, sesame seeds, and white mustard seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, at the three junctions of the day for seven nights. They will become submissive.

[These] come to pass. Having consecrated water, ashes, or mustard seeds one of these with eight thousand recitations, one should scatter them in the four directions; thus the binding of the mandala is accomplished. One should offer eight thousand oblations of milk; one is liberated from disease. One who desires food should offer food. Having ascended a mountain peak, subsisting on alms...
One should recite [the mantra] three hundred thousand times. At the conclusion, having fasted for three nights and kindled a fire beneath an *aśvattha* tree,
one should offer oblations throughout the entire night of parched grains smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.

One becomes a king. By offering sesame seeds and ghee into the fire, all aims are accomplished. One should offer honey; one becomes beloved by all people. One should offer ghee; one becomes radiant. One should offer milk; peace ensues. One should offer curd; nourishment ensues. Having kindled the fire with *sinduvāra* wood, one should offer the first portion of every herb.
Food becomes inexhaustible just as it was prepared. One obtains the binding of a turban (the insignia of royalty) for whomsoever one desires.

One should offer a hundred thousand *nimba* flowers; one becomes beloved by all people. One should offer a hundred thousand unbroken grains of *śāli* rice; one obtains a village. Having kindled a fire with *aśoka* wood, [one should offer] a hundred thousand...

One should perform oblations. By doing so, one obtains a kingdom over a single region. While burning *agaru* incense before the cloth painting (*paṭa*), one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times; thereafter, the royal palace shall come under one's control. Subsisting on alms or on sacrificial food (*haviṣya*), one should recite it forty-nine hundred thousand times; one will obtain sovereignty over the earth. Having subsisted on milk and barley gruel...
One should recite [the mantra] eight hundred thousand times. One should offer one hundred thousand white mustard seeds; one will obtain the sovereignty of a neighboring kingdom.

One should perform a fire-oblation of one hundred thousand young shoots of *dūrvā* grass; one becomes long-lived. One should perform a fire-oblation of one hundred thousand mango leaves smeared with milk; one is liberated from all diseases. All grains gathered in one place...

Having performed [the preliminary rites], one should offer a hundred thousand oblations; all grains will become inexhaustible. One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of *madhūka* wood; wealth will arise. Having combined realgar, yellow orpiment, and *daṃśarocanā*, and having consecrated it eight thousand times before the cloth-painting (*paṭa*), one should place it upon leaves of *bodhi*-tree wood and recite the mantra.

Success is attained. Whichever woman or man to whom it is given becomes subject to one's will. One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of clarified butter; one obtains three villages. One should recite [the mantra] ten million times; one becomes a *vidyādhara* with a retinue of a hundred. One should recite it one hundred thousand times; one obtains delicious food and drink without having asked for it. One becomes the sovereign of the seven continents.
One comes under one's control. One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of *arka* fuel-sticks; there will be the binding of a royal turban (*paṭṭabandha*).
By means of ritual cleansing (*apāmārjana*), one removes eye disease. For one afflicted by fever, there is cleansing with *kuśa* grass.
One should tie on a thread spun by a maiden and consecrated a hundred times; one becomes fortunate. [The same applies to] collyrium.

Those desiring to accomplish [this rite] should take one *pala* of *sauvīrāñjana*, heat it over a fire until it becomes fragrant, and purify it through the ritual of collyrium (*añjanāparikarma*). Then, during a lunar eclipse, entering the water, one should recite the mantra until the substance becomes a *kūṣmāṇḍa* fruit. At that very moment it bursts open; as soon as it has burst open, the practitioner becomes radiant with the brilliance of a weapon.
Kuṇḍalamantreśvara is the master of all vidyās; it is invincible and its movement is unimpeded. ... [it] flies up.

One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of *palāśa* wood; one obtains a thousand pieces of gold. Having fasted for three nights and subsisting on milk and barley-gruel, one should perform the rite of accomplishment.

(Taking one *pala* of realgar [manaḥśilā] and placing it upon seven leaves of the *aśvattha* tree, one should recite the mantra until it bursts into flames. Having split open one's body, one should cast it [into the fire]; at that very moment, he rises up. He becomes a *vidyādhara*.)* (PDF 172, p. 710)
One becomes [endowed with] unimpeded divine, stainless ears and the speed of thought, possessing the color of the rising sun, highly esteemed by all *vidyādharas*,

moving through divine realms as a *vidyādhara* with a retinue of a hundred. Having performed a magnificent worship with perfumes and flowers before the cloth painting (*paṭa*), subsisting on milk and barley-gruel, dressed in clean garments and lower robes, he who—

Whatever one prays for, that one obtains. During a lunar eclipse, having performed worship beneath a Bodhi tree with perfumes, flowers, and incense, one should recite the mantra twenty-one times over realgar and yellow orpiment, rub them upon one's head, and apply a mark (tilaka) on the forehead. One may then enter the royal court and become a favorite of the king.

It happens as follows: one should offer eight thousand oblations of lotus seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. By uttering the name of whomever [one desires], that person becomes submissive. A celibate practitioner who has conquered the senses should perform a homa of agallochum and frankincense. On the full moon day, [one should bathe] the king with four jars filled with water over which the mantra has been recited eight thousand times.

Or one should bathe a high-ranking official; he will become prosperous. For one who is incurable, having kindled a fire with *kṣīra* fuel-sticks, one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of curds, honey, and ghee, or perform a *homa* with red and blue lotuses or *jātī* flowers. In front of the cloth painting, one should subsist on a diet of milk and barley-gruel.

Worship should be performed with increasing offerings; the monks should be fed. By this rite, even that which is unattainable becomes accomplished. One who desires wealth obtains riches by performing a fire-oblation (*homa*) with *apāmārga* fuel-sticks. Through a fire-oblation of clarified butter, there is pacification (*śāntika*) and nourishment (*pauṣṭika*). Or, one may perform a fire-oblation of eight thousand *guggulu* resin sticks smeared with curd, honey, and clarified butter, using lotuses.
In this way, all objectives are accomplished. If one offers oblations after reciting the mantra over black rice (*kṛṣṇavrīhi*) dedicated to a specific person, that person becomes submissive.

Subjugation is also achieved with fuel-sticks of *apāmārga*. Having kindled a fire with *bilva* wood in front of the cloth painting (*paṭa*), one should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *agaru* (aloe-wood) fuel-sticks; it grants all objectives at a shrine containing relics (*sadhātuka-caitya*).
One should offer ten thousand oblations; one obtains a kingdom. By offering one hundred thousand oblations of lotuses, one becomes possessed of great wealth.
Having performed worship for all these oblations with perfumes, flowers, and incense, one should begin the fire sacrifice.
Having kindled the fire with eight hundred *bilva* wood sticks, [one should offer] those sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.

One should offer eight thousand oblations of *bilva* fuel-sticks. Having kindled [the fire], one should offer [oblations] of *agaru* fuel-sticks at a reliquary (*caitya*) containing relics, with perfumes, flowers, and incense. Having first become pure as previously described, one should kindle the fire.
One should offer oblations of *āgakesara* and *priyaṅgu* [flowers]. By means of the inner vital breath (*prāṇa*), one obtains wealth.
(pdf 173, p.
718) Having kindled the fire with *palāśa* wood, one should offer oblations of *vaikaṅkana* fuel-sticks smeared with curd, honey, and clarified butter.

One should offer oblations; one obtains a thousand gold pieces. Having kindled a fire with *udumbara* wood, one should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *vāmaka* fuel-sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
Having consecrated [the object] one hundred thousand times and bound it upon the hand, one becomes undefeated in battle. [If bound] on the head...
Bound by it, one becomes invisible. Having gone to the river Kṛṣṇaprapañcā, one should cast eight thousand white flowers into the current; as many as eighty-eight thousand dīnāras one obtains.
This same rite applies to *kunduruka* and also to *bilva*; it bestows enjoyments as well.

On the fifth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for a day and night before a painted image, one should place *gorocanā* on a white cloth and recite the mantra until threefold success is attained. If it moves at the feet of the practitioner, he lives for seven thousand years. If it blazes, he becomes one who endures for an eon (*kalpa*). It cures all diseases; with clay, it effects binding and release.

The binding of the maṇḍala: one should offer eight thousand oblations of lotuses before the cloth painting at the three junctions of the day for seven days; one will see a treasure. Before the cloth painting, one should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *śatapuṣpā* flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee; one obtains a kingdom. [One should also offer] one hundred thousand oblations of ghee.
One should offer oblations; one obtains five villages. One should offer eight thousand *arka* flowers;
one obtains a thousand gold coins (*rūpaka*). While reciting [the mantra], it grants everything, with the exception of that which is associated with sensual desire.
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for the night, one should [offer] *nirmālya* before the noble Mañjuśrī at night.
One should offer ten thousand oblations of items smeared with curd, honey, and ghee; one obtains great prosperity.

Beneath a Bodhi tree, one should offer eight thousand oblations of fuel-sticks from a Bodhi tree; one obtains a thousand gold coins (*rūpaka*). One should offer eight thousand *jāti* flowers three times a day for seven nights.

One obtains a thousand gold pieces. By performing these rites, having fasted for three nights, one should kindle a fire at the foot of a Bodhi tree with fuel-sticks of milkwood and offer eight thousand oblations of guggulu resin pills the size of cotton seeds;
one obtains a thousand dīnāras. For eye diseases, fever, abdominal tumors, headaches, and sciatica, [the medicine] should be administered after reciting the mantra over it.

Protection must be performed by means of this very [mantra] against all fears and calamities arising from wolves, tigers, buffaloes, crocodiles, elephants, bears, thieves, snakes, piśācas, bhūtas, brahmarākṣasas, and other such [beings]. Having gone to a lotus pond,
one should grind [the substance] with human milk, perform a thousand [recitations], nourish it, and offer five pills as an oblation.

Having performed the bali offering in front of the cloth painting (paṭa), one should place [the substance] in a casket and recite the mantra until the mustard seeds crackle; at that time, (174, p. 719) [one should know: "It has been accomplished."

It brings about the subjugation of all sentient beings. If it smokes, one becomes the king of all those who possess the power of invisibility; one lives for infinite eons. If, however, it blazes forth, then one becomes a king of the Vidyādharas, like a divine youth (*devakumāra*), with a radiance equal to the rising sun, remaining for a great eon (*mahākalpa*). The same procedure applies to *rocanā*, yellow orpiment (*haritāla*), and so forth.

These are to be accomplished. For all [practitioners], there are three kinds of success (*siddhi*). One who desires to perform pacification (*śānti*) should kindle a fire with sacrificial fuel sticks (*samidh*) and offer eight thousand oblations of *paramānna* for three nights; pacification will occur.
For oneself or another, or for a village or city in the event of drought, one should offer the "three sweets" (*trimadhura*) for seven nights.

Having consecrated the conch, banner, and so forth, one exhausts [the effects of] karma; within seven days, one exhausts even the five sins of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*). One becomes capable of all ritual actions (*sarvakarmasamartha*). For binding by means of a *vidyā*, a knot should be made with a thread over which the mantra has been recited twenty-one times. Binding the perimeter of the maṇḍala is done with mustard seeds. During a lunar or solar eclipse, [one should use] sandalwood...

Having smeared a mandala and placed equal portions of ghee, honey, and *āmalakī* juice in a copper vessel, one should sit in the cross-legged posture (*paryaṅka*) and recite the mantra until it becomes warm. Having drunk that, one becomes a possessor of a retentive memory (*śrutidhara*).

One who observes the fast (*poṣadhika*) should, at the improper time, recite the mantra seven times over a mouthful of water and drink it; whatever one intends while performing this, that shall come to pass.

He speaks within a dream: "Having recited the *śvetavacā* seven times and placed it between the teeth in the mouth, whatever one asks for, that one obtains; one becomes a superior debater. Having focused the mind upon whichever state [one desires] and recited [the mantra], one should offer flowers, incense, and so forth before the Tathāgata, and cast a directional offering (*diśābali*) toward the four quarters."

Then, seated upon a bundle of *kuśa* grass, one should recite [the mantra] eight thousand times; this fulfills all desires. Having fashioned a lion out of earth from an anthill and anointed it with *gorocanā*, one who has performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*) should place a ball of food before the cloth painting and recite it three hundred thousand times. Then it moves; as soon as it moves, [success is attained].
And he becomes accomplished. At that very moment, while reciting the mantra, one should mount a lion.
With hair curled in locks, having the appearance of a sixteen-year-old—though being sixteen years old—one flies up.
Having approached all the vidyādharas, even unto Brahmā, and being immortal, one is reborn among the gods. Having seen [this],...

Upon hearing it, one causes the enemy army to be paralyzed. Having prepared a jar completely filled with water scented with all types of rice and having covered its mouth with mango sprouts, one should bathe Vināyaka with [the water] consecrated eight times;
he will quickly release [the obstruction]. She becomes disciplined... she gives birth easily. [One should treat] all planetary spirits...

For the subjugation of great feudal lords (*mahāsāmanta*), one should offer eight thousand oblations of *arka* wood fuel smeared with curd, honey, and ghee before the cloth painting (*paṭa*) for seven nights at the three junctions of the day (morning, noon, and evening).

One becomes master over [the person] together with their retinue. One should offer eight thousand *priyaṅgu* flowers into the fire for seven days for a princess; she will be given to him. One should offer eight thousand oil-cakes at the three junctions of the day for seven nights;

this brings even one standing before them under one's control. Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times at a shrine containing relics.

Subsisting on alms, one should then fast for one night on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight; having performed worship of the cloth-painting according to one’s means, one should offer eight thousand oblations of black sesame seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
Then, at dawn, one obtains a village. [If] twelve [villages are desired], [one should perform it] until success; [for] non-success, [the rite requires] a thousand lumps [of sesame] for a village.

Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), one who subsists on water and barley-meal should install the cloth-painting facing west on the bank of a river; having performed worship according to one's means, having lit twenty-one lamps including a lamp of ghee, and having offered an outer oblation (*bali*) for all spirits (*sārvabhūtika*); he attains [the result].
Seated in the paryanka posture, one should recite [the mantra] until the divine son Aruṇa arrives; he grants a boon.

One should subsist on alms and recite for three months beneath a *vaṭa* tree. Then, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having smeared a sacrificial ground (*sthaṇḍilaka*) the size of a cow-hide, one should offer a *bali* sacrifice consisting of all flavorful substances outside.

Having offered a bali-oblation consisting of all [ingredients], one should then sit upon a bundle of kuśa grass and offer eight thousand oblations of guggulu resin pills, the size of jujube seeds, into smokeless embers. Thereupon, the yakṣiṇī Paṭavāsinī arrives. One should offer her an argha with scented water, and she says, "What shall I do?"—she is a mother.

The sister says, "One of these must be taken. She gives a *rasāyana* elixir; having consumed it, one becomes long-lived for an eon (*kalpa*) and gains the strength of a *yakṣa*. Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), having made offerings according to one's means at a reliquary (*caitya*) containing relics, bathing three times a day, and reciting the mantra an immeasurable number of times during the three junctions of the day for six months.

Subsisting on alms or on a diet of milk and barley-gruel, one should then begin the practice. During the dark fortnight, under the asterism Puṣya, having purchased *karavīrikā* realgar from a hero’s sale, one should purify it with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*).
Then, having given the medicinal herb to a Brahmin girl, one should have her bathe and adorned herself.

Having entered facing the east, one should grind [the substance] during an auspicious lunar day, astrological division (*karana*), and moment (*muhurta*). Having made an uneven pill the size of a jujube stone with the ring finger, and having placed it in a casket of *aśvattha* wood, one should perform a thousand oblations before the cloth-painting. Having fasted for three nights and observed the vow, at the end of the bright fortnight, one should perform a grand worship.

Having prepared a most magnificent offering and presented it, having honored it with perfumes, flowers, and incense, having placed it in a casket, having established it with four [mantras] and covered it with three, and having supported it with his hand,
he should pay homage to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas and recite the mantra while seated upon a bundle of *kuśa* grass.

As long as they offer substances such as [the aforementioned items], he departs once more. Half-jewels [and other materials] are required for the rite. Then, if he remains right there, no fear of Vaiṣṇavas shall arise.
One sees the Blessed Maitreya. Having made a vow, one should enter. This wards off all obstacles.

In a clean place, one should cast a house of dust upon a mustard seed; thus all obstacles are warded off. If one desires to travel swiftly, one should say, "Go! and, having fashioned a clay seal on the hem of one's garment...
Having consecrated [the substance] eight thousand times and placed it upon the bitten person, one should summon [the poison]. Even one who is dead shall rise up.

Having purified substances such as realgar (*manaḥśilā*) and so forth, or weapons such as the sword, discus, and *musuṇḍī*, with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), and having performed a *sahasra-sampāta* oblation, one should take whichever substance [is desired] on the full moon day.

Having drawn the *sādhana*-maṇḍala upon a cloth and placed the substance [to be sought] upon it, one should sit in the *paryaṅka* posture and recite the mantra until success (*siddhi*) is attained. On a wooden board, having written the name of whichever substance one desires and having consecrated it eight thousand times, it should be thrown into a lake where a *nāga* resides; then that *nāga* [will grant the object].

It accomplishes everything. Within seven days, it certainly accomplishes the desired object. Having written the name of the person to be invoked upon a wooden board with substances such as [incense] powder, one should likewise cast it into a well or a lake.
Then, a man should be made to submerge into the water. He hears a great sound from within that [water], saying: "In such-and-such a place..."

In a particular location where substances and such are situated, one should take them from there. When crossing a river and so forth, or in the presence of the ten [directions], in an assembly, in a royal court, or in a dispute, one should recollect [the mantra]; in all cases, one becomes unconquered. If one wishes to bring someone under one's control, one should visualize Noble Mañjuśrī in that person’s mouth and engage in some conversation with them.
In a short time, one comes under control. Having placed water in a vessel, one should meditate upon Noble Mañjuśrī.

With that water, consecrated eight thousand times, one should visualize the bitten person; he becomes free from poison. Then, having entered the maṇḍala according to the prescribed procedure, one should take cow dung that has fallen [from the udder] of a bull in full milk.

Subsisting on sacrificial food (*haviṣya*) and observing silence, one should form a mandala and perform recitation (*japa*). Beginning on the full moon day, one should continue the recitation until the third *lakṣa* is reached. A celibate student (*brahmacārī*) should observe this vow for six months. Success is attained here within a month;
after six months, the black world becomes manifest even to the physical body. One attains the supreme...
One attains accomplishment; in brief, one accomplishes every mantra.
From the *Mahākalparāja*, the *Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa*, the sixtieth chapter (*paṭala*), the section on the accomplishment of gold (*hemasādhana*),
the expansion, the conclusion, is finished.
And thus the ritual procedure (kalpa) for [the deity] Yathāla********** is completed.

(Svasti) May there be well-being! Written by the presiding authority of the Śrīmūlaghoṣa Monastery, while residing in [Śrī]rāṅgala, on the [blank] day of the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, under the lunar mansion [blank], and while Jupiter was situated in Leo; thus the Mañjuśrīkalpa is completed.
"Written by Paṇḍita Ravi-candra, who departed from Madhyadeśa, for the sake of Śrīvo...
May there be auspiciousness!"
